{
  "__comment": [
    "Master calendar / time definition. Loaded once at boot by the WorldClock autoload.",
    "WorldClock is authoritative for the whole simulation - no other system tracks its own",
    "day/season/hour counter (see docs/10_core_foundation/11_overview.md and 13_architecture.md).",
    "",
    "This file is DATA ONLY (JSON = what things are). Timer advancement, signal emission, and",
    "speed control live in WorldClock.gd (GDScript = what things do).",
    "",
    "Keys beginning with '__' are documentation comments and are skipped by the loader.",
    "",
    "FIELDS:",
    "  time_scale.real_seconds_per_game_hour - wall-clock seconds per in-game hour at x1 speed",
    "  time_scale.hours_per_day / days_per_season / seasons_per_year - calendar structure",
    "  season_order      - canonical cycle; index into this drives day_of_year()",
    "  start             - new-game calendar position (matches WorldClock.gd defaults today)",
    "  event_times       - named time-of-day events in HOURS. Shared by the clock AND every sky/fog",
    "                      curve in data/sky/sky_settings.json (curves key against these names).",
    "  day_length_curve  - seasonal day-length cosine from 11_overview.md S5. day_of_year 0-111;",
    "                      summer solstice (longest day) at day 28, winter solstice at day 84.",
    "                      daylight_hours(doy) = mean - amplitude * cos((doy - summer_solstice)/112 * TAU)",
    "",
    "NOTE: rise/set 'peak' sub-events (sunrise_peak_start, etc.) used by Stonehearth are NOT defined",
    "here yet. For v1, sky curves key only against the 8 base events below. If a softer shoulder is",
    "needed later, add a 'rise_set_length_hours' field and derive peak events in WorldClock."
  ],

  "time_scale": {
    "real_seconds_per_game_hour": 60,
    "hours_per_day": 24,
    "days_per_season": 28,
    "seasons_per_year": 4
  },

  "season_order": ["spring", "summer", "autumn", "winter"],

  "start": { "year": 1, "season": "summer", "day": 1, "hour": 8.0 },

  "event_times": {
    "midnight":      0,
    "sunrise_start": 5,
    "sunrise":       6,
    "sunrise_end":   7,
    "midday":        14,
    "sunset_start":  20,
    "sunset":        21,
    "sunset_end":    22
  },

  "day_length_curve": {
    "mean_hours":          12.0,
    "amplitude_hours":     4.0,
    "summer_solstice_doy": 28,
    "winter_solstice_doy": 84
  }
}

{
  "__comment": [
    "Camera configuration. Source of truth for Camera.gd (21_camera.md).",
    "Feel ported from Stonehearth's player_camera_controller.lua (verified source 2026-06-07).",
    "  Real SH constants: _min_zoom 15, _max_zoom 300; zoom step = distance-to-cursor * factor",
    "  (factor 0.2 <100u / 0.3 <500u / 0.4 else); MIN_X_ANGLE 5, MAX_X_ANGLE 80 above horizon;",
    "  mouse_orbit_sensitivity 0.26; pan speed = camera position.y (height-proportional).",
    "Deepdraft uses NEGATIVE pitch (look-down): -90 = straight down, 0 = horizon, so Stonehearth's",
    "  5..80 above-horizon maps to -5 (shallow) .. -80 (steep) here, default -50.",
    "ZOOM (21_camera.md): proportional notch = zoom_step_fraction * current distance",
    "  (geometric zoom). zoom_speed is the non-proportional fixed-step fallback only.",
    "  min_distance 2 / cursor_min_gap 1.5 allow ground-level close-up; the surface floor",
    "  (surface_floor_* keys) prevents clipping instead of a hard min distance."
  ],

  "camera_settings": {
    "fov": 45.0,
    "near_clip": 0.1,
    "far_clip": 1024.0,
    "default_position": { "x": 512.0, "y": 70.0, "z": 512.0 },

  },

  "rotation": {

    "invert_y": false,
    "min_pitch": -80.0,

    "proportional": true,

source_text.data/furniture/door.json:
{
  "__comment": [
    "Door - the doc 22 prerequisite for doc 34's sealed-room detection.",
    "",
    "RESIZED 2026-08-06 (Alen playtest feedback): footprint is 2x1 (was 1x1),",
    "visually 2 blocks wide x 4 blocks tall - the original single-tile slab",
    "read as out-of-proportion next to 3-tall dwarves and 1-wide corridors.",
    "Both footprint cells matter for sealing: RoomManager now registers EVERY",
    "footprint cell a door occupies as a sealing boundary (not just the",
    "origin cell), so a 2-wide door only seals a room if BOTH tiles stop the",
    "flood-fill - see FurniturePlacementController._install/_teardown_installed",
    "passing component.cells (the full footprint) to on_furniture_changed(),",
    "and RoomManager.on_furniture_changed()'s updated 'cells: Array[Vector3i]'",
    "signature.",
    "",
    "COLLISION_REGIONS IS DELIBERATELY EMPTY. Every other furniture piece uses",
    "collision_regions to register NavGrid-blocking occupancy (see",
    "FurniturePlacementController._install). A door must stay walkable, so it",
    "carries no occupancy boxes at all - placing one changes nothing about",
    "pathing. It IS still footprint-tracked (blocks a stockpile zone from being",
    "drawn on the same tile, which you wouldn't want anyway) and IS tracked by",
    "RoomManager as a sealing boundary via the direct on_furniture_changed()",
    "call FurniturePlacementController makes on install/uninstall.",
    "",
    "Per doc 34: 'Dwarves always close doors behind them. Door blocks are",
    "always treated as sealed for temperature calculation purposes regardless",
    "of animation state.' v1 has no open/close animation at all - every",
    "installed door is permanently 'closed' for sealing purposes, which is a",
    "strict superset of that rule (always-sealed is always at least as sealed",
    "as 'sealed except when a dwarf is mid-walk-through').",
    "",
    "PLACEMENT: v1 has no doorway validation (no check that the door sits",
    "between two solid walls) - only the standard NavGrid.is_walkable(cell)",
    "check every floor piece gets. Place doors sensibly; a door in the open",
    "does nothing (RoomManager's flood-fill will simply fail to find a",
    "bounded interior on either side of it)."
  ],
  "furniture_key": "base:furniture:door",
  "furniture_category": "door",
  "display_name": "Door",
  "description": "A stout double plank door on iron hinges. Dwarves pass through freely; it seals the room for warmth.",
  "model": "res://assets/models/furniture/door.glb",
  "item_key": "base:resources:furniture:door",
  "placement": "floor",
  "yaw_steps": 4,
  "footprint": {
    "width": 2,
    "depth": 1
  },
  "blocks_movement": false,
  "collision_regions": [],

  "room_anchor": false
}

source_text.data/furniture/trade_counter.json:
{
  "__comment": [
	"STATUS (2026-10-01, art doc 37): model, floor placement, packed item, fetch/build",
	"and uninstall are live. Shop designation, merchant visits, buy/sell orders and",
	"reputation fields below remain future design data; no trading behavior is enabled.",
	"The following room/trade rules describe that future system, not current behavior.",
	"",
	"Trade Counter — the room-anchor furniture piece that designates a sealed room as a Shop.",
	"This is the first furniture definition in the game. Its schema establishes the pattern",
	"for all future furniture items.",
	"",
	"ROOM DESIGNATION:",
	"  A sealed room (enclosed walls + one or more doors) containing a Trade Counter",
	"  is automatically designated as a 'shop' room. The room type is re-evaluated",
	"  whenever any furniture is added to or removed from the room.",
	"  Only one Trade Counter per room is valid. A second counter invalidates the room",
	"  designation until one is removed.",
	"",
	"ROOM VALIDATION:",
	"  A shop room may only contain items whose furniture_category is listed in",
	"  room_compatible_categories. If any item with a category in",
	"  room_invalidating_categories is placed inside the room, the Shop designation",
	"  is immediately removed. The room reverts to an undesignated room until the",
	"  offending item is removed.",
	"  See furniture_category field on each furniture item for its category string.",
	"",
	"SELL SIDE (automated):",
	"  All items stored in room_compatible storage units inside the shop room are",
	"  automatically available for sale when a merchant visits. The merchant checks",
	"  each item against their want list and buys matching stock at",
	"  base_trade_value ± demand_modifier. The colony receives gold coins equal to",
	"  the transaction total. Sold items are removed from shop storage immediately.",
	"",
	"BUY ORDERS (player-configured, automated):",
	"  The player configures buy orders on the Trade Counter via the UI.",
	"  Schema per order: { item_id, max_count, max_price_per_unit }",
	"  When a merchant carries an item matching a buy order:",
	"    - The colony buys as many units as available up to max_count.",
	"    - If gold coin balance is insufficient for the full order, partial fill applies:",
	"      buy as many units as coins allow at the stated price.",
	"    - Purchased goods are placed in available shop room storage first.",
	"      If shop storage is full, goods are dropped on the shop floor.",
	"    - Dwarves then haul floor goods to appropriate colony stockpiles.",
	"  Buy orders persist indefinitely and re-evaluate on every merchant visit.",
	"  Default: empty array (no buy orders). Configured per save, not in this file.",
	"",
	"COIN FLOW:",
	"  Net coins = coins received from sales − coins spent on buy orders.",
	"  If net is positive, gold coins are added to the nearest stockpile_currency stockpile",
	"  or dropped at the Trade Counter if none exists.",
	"  If net is negative (buy orders exceed sale revenue in a single visit),",
	"  the deficit is drawn from the colony's existing coin stockpile.",
	"  If the colony cannot cover the deficit, buy orders are partially filled",
	"  until coins run out.",
	"",
	"MERCHANT VISIT CONDITION:",
	"  Merchants will only stop at the colony if a valid shop room exists AND the",
	"  shop has at least one item in storage OR at least one active buy order.",
	"  A shop room with a Trade Counter but no stock and no buy orders is treated",
	"  as inactive — caravans pass by without stopping.",
	"",
	"TRADE NOTIFICATION:",
	"  On trade completion a summary toast is posted:",
	"    'Trade complete — sold X items, bought Y items, net +Z coins.'",
    "  Full transaction log is accessible from the Trade Counter inspect panel."
  ],

  "furniture_key": "base:furniture:trade_counter",
  "furniture_category": "trade",
  "display_name": "Trade Counter",
  "description": "A dressed-stone counter with iron edging and a carved front panel.",
  "model": "res://assets/models/furniture/trade_counter.glb",
  "item_key": "base:resources:furniture:trade_counter",
  "placement": "floor",
  "yaw_steps": 4,
  "footprint": { "width": 2, "depth": 1 },
  "blocks_movement": true,

  "__comment_collision": [
	"collision_regions defines one or more axis-aligned boxes in furniture-local block coordinates.",
	"Origin (0,0,0) = bottom-front-left corner of the footprint. Y is up. Units are game blocks (0.5 m).",
	"Each region is read by the furniture placement system to create CollisionShape3D nodes at runtime.",
	"Multi-region is used when different parts of the piece have different heights (e.g. beds).",
    "A single region covering the full footprint at the correct visual height is the common case."
  ],
  "collision_regions": [
	{ "min": [0, 0, 0], "max": [2, 2, 1] }
  ],

  "room_anchor": true,
  "room_type": "shop",
  "max_per_room": 1,

  "room_compatible_categories": [
	"trade",
	"storage",
    "decorative"
  ],

  "room_invalidating_categories": [
	"bed",
	"workshop",
    "production"
  ],

  "sell_source": "room_storage",

  "purchased_goods_destination": "room_storage_or_floor",

  "buy_orders_schema": {
	"__comment": "Runtime schema — buy orders are saved per-colony, not defined here.",

{
  "__comment": [
    "Default / clear-day sky master. Loaded by the SkyController autoload.",
    "Trimmed Forward+ equivalent of Stonehearth's data/calendar/sky_settings.json; colour and",
    "height_fog numbers below are seeded directly from Stonehearth's validated sunny settings.",
    "",
    "DATA ONLY. Per-frame interpolation between keyframes lives in SkyController.gd. Weather files",
    "(data/weather/*.json) override only the deltas of this base via their 'sky_overrides' block.",
    "",
    "Keys beginning with '__' are documentation comments and are skipped by the loader.",
    "",
    "KEYFRAME SHAPE: every curve is an array of { \"at\": <event_name>, ... } points. 'at' must be",
    "one of the event_times in data/calendar/calendar.json. SkyController expands event names to",
    "seconds, sorts, and interpolates; the curve wraps from the last point back to the first.",
    "",
    "CELESTIALS (sun, moon): each directional light has:",
    "  light_color   [r,g,b] 0-1  - emitted colour; (0,0,0) => light switched OFF (this is how the",
    "                               sun 'sets' and the moon 'rises'). Also tints the fog (see below).",
    "  ambient_color [r,g,b] 0-1  - ambient/fill contribution at that time",
    "  angle_pitch   degrees      - sun arc: 0 at horizon (sunrise) -> -90 overhead (midday) ->",
    "                               -180 (sunset). Yaw/roll are fixed on the light node for v1.",
    "",
    "HEIGHT FOG: [fog_height, thickness, noise, distance] keyed by event. THIS IS THE SKY/FOG MATCH:",
    "  fog colour is taken from the active celestial light colour, so sky and fog always agree",
    "  (docs/20_player_interface/24_world_rendering.md). Mapping to Godot Environment:",
    "    fog_height - world Y below which ground fog accumulates (0 = none). Volumetric-fog height term.",
    "    thickness  - fog density / opacity                          -> Environment.fog_density",
    "    noise      - animated noise breakup strength (cosmetic; defer) ",
    "    distance   - MAX honest view distance in world units        -> Environment.fog_depth_end",
    "                 (final cap = min(distance, render budget from doc 06))",
    "",
    "STARFIELD: brightness 0 in daylight, 1 at night; drives the star layer / night sky tint.",
    "",
    "SKY GRADIENT: if the faithful [time x height] sky-shader route is chosen (08_sky_plan.md Q4),",
    "the per-weather gradient PNG path lives on the weather file, not here. If instead ProceduralSky",
    "colours are driven from data, add a 'sky_gradient_colors' block here keyed to the same events.",

    "now lives in data with no visual change. Phase 2 will animate sky_*_color / fog_light_color /",

  },

    "PHASE 2 day/night sky. top / horizon / ground_bottom colours keyed by event name.",
    "SkyController evaluates these against WorldClock.hour each frame and drives the",

  ],

      { "at": "midnight",      "rgb": [0.03, 0.04, 0.10] },

{
  "__comment": [
    "Task scheduler tunables (doc 16 First Dwarf Milestone, §2). Loaded by the",
    "TaskManager autoload — no other script reads this file (Registry Pattern).",
    "JSON = what things are (the numbers); GDScript = what things do (the loop).",
    "",
    "NO-HANG CONTRACT (doc 16 §2.5 — these keys ARE the guarantees):",
    "  scheduler_budget_usec   - hard time budget per scheduler wake; the matching",
    "                            loop stops mid-scan when exceeded and resumes from",
    "                            its cursor on the next wake. Overload degrades into",
    "                            assignment LATENCY, never frame time.",
    "  max_probes_per_wake     - reachability probes per wake, whichever limit hits",
    "                            first. Probes are the only non-trivial loop cost.",
    "  probe_node_cap          - A* expansion cap per probe (doc 32: 200). A capped",
    "                            failure counts as unreachable -> backoff.",
    "  heartbeat_interval_s    - slow safety-net poll; normal operation is",
    "                            event-driven wakes (task added, dwarf idle, ...).",
    "  backoff_base_s / backoff_max_s - unreachable-task retry curve:",
    "                            min(backoff_base^blocked_count, backoff_max).",
    "  unreachable_signal_threshold - consecutive blocked probes before",
    "                            task_unreachable fires (doc 31: 3).",
    "",
    "  static_priorities       - per-type base priority (doc 31 table). Stored on",
    "                            the task at creation; colony bonuses are computed",
    "                            per wake per TYPE and never written into tasks.",
    "",
    "Keys beginning with '__' are documentation comments and are skipped."
  ],

  "scheduler": {
    "scheduler_budget_usec": 1000,
    "max_probes_per_wake": 8,
    "probe_node_cap": 1200,
    "heartbeat_interval_s": 0.5,
    "backoff_base_s": 2.0,
    "backoff_max_s": 30.0,

FETCH_BUILD 45 > HAUL 40: SH-verified - the placement task group's priority band TOPS restock's (0.93 vs 0.8), installing furniture outranks putting things away. build/uninstall_time_s: the work-swing duration at the ghost / installed piece.",

{
  "__comment": [
    "Weather definition. Loaded by the WeatherManager autoload. One file per weather type.",
    "BASE + OVERRIDE model: a weather file overrides only the deltas of data/sky/sky_settings.json",
    "via 'sky_overrides'. 'clear' is the baseline weather and overrides nothing.",
    "",
    "DATA ONLY. Selection (weighted per season), scheduling, and the gradient/curve crossfade live",
    "in WeatherManager.gd / SkyController.gd.",
    "",
    "FIELDS:",
    "  id                           - namespaced weather key (used by data/calendar/weather_schedule.json)",
    "  display_name                 - UI label",
    "  vision_multiplier            - GAMEPLAY sight/streaming radius scale (1.0 = full). Separate from",
    "                                 the fog 'distance' look; multiplies WorldRenderer view radius and",
    "                                 camera far clip (ties weather to the doc-06 streaming budget).",
    "  is_dark_during_daytime       - dims daytime ambient (overcast/storm feel)",
    "  hide_cloud_shadows           - suppress moving cloud shadow projector (future)",
    "  snow_accumulation_per_minute - per game-minute snow cover delta; negative = melt/decay",
    "  sky_gradient                 - per-weather sky gradient PNG (faithful sky-shader route only; ",
    "                                 omit if driving ProceduralSky colours from data)",
    "  sky_overrides                - partial sky_settings.json (only the curves that differ from base)",
    "  thoughts                     - mood thoughts applied to dwarves while active (see 41_dwarf_agents.md)",
    "",
    "Keys beginning with '__' are documentation comments and are skipped by the loader."
  ],

  "id": "base:weather:clear",
  "display_name": "Clear",
  "vision_multiplier": 1.0,
  "is_dark_during_daytime": false,
  "hide_cloud_shadows": false,
  "snow_accumulation_per_minute": -0.0007,
  "sky_gradient": "res://assets/sky/gradients/clear.png",
  "sky_overrides": {},
  "thoughts": []
}

{
  "__comment": [
    "Aging Cellar — deep underground workshop for barrel-conditioning premium drinks.",
    "",
    "TEMPERATURE REQUIREMENT (see docs/30_simulation_systems/34_temperature.md):",
    "  The aging cellar block must be placed inside a *sealed room* whose computed",
    "  temperature falls within the recipe's temp_range_c. Temperature is determined",
    "  by the room's mean floor Y plus any heat bonus from torches or braziers placed",
    "  inside the sealed room.",
    "",
    "  progress_pauses_out_of_range: true",
    "    → When the room's temperature falls outside a recipe's temp_range_c, that",
    "      recipe's aging progress bar PAUSES. Progress is not lost. Aging resumes",
    "      automatically once temperature is restored to the valid range.",
    "    → This applies even mid-batch. A torch removed from the room during aging",
    "      may drop temperature below the minimum; the batch pauses until a torch",
    "      is replaced.",
    "",
    "  No cooling mechanic exists. If a room is too warm for a recipe, the player",
    "  must build a new aging cellar at greater depth.",
    "  If a room is too cold, placing torches inside the sealed room raises its",
    "  temperature. See 34_temperature.md for the heat_units formula.",
    "",
    "PLACEMENT:",
    "  The aging cellar block may be placed at any Y, but its recipes will only",
    "  be available if the sealed room's computed temperature is within range.",
    "  There is no hard placement constraint on Y — temperature is the gating factor.",
    "",
    "AGING PROCESS (two-phase, passive):",
    "  1. LOAD  — A dwarf hauls inputs to the cellar and spends work_time loading.",
    "  2. AGE   — The cellar ages autonomously for aging_time in-game hours.",
    "             No dwarf needed. Progress bar visible in workshop UI.",
    "             Progress pauses if room temperature leaves temp_range_c.",
    "  3. COLLECT — When aging_time elapses (accumulated while in-range), a COLLECT",
    "               task auto-queues. A dwarf retrieves the output to a stockpile.",
    "",
    "  Only one batch per cellar block may be in progress at a time.",
    "  Build multiple aging cellar blocks for parallel production.",
    "",
    "RECIPE TEMPERATURE RANGES (cold mountain gradient — see 34_temperature.md):",
    "  Vintage Wine  : 6–10°C  → Cool Cave zone   (Y 57–75 baseline)",

    "  Frozen Vault  : ≤ 0°C   → Y ≤ 35 baseline — too cold for all aging",
    "  (Torches can raise base depth temp into range — see 34_temperature.md)"

{
  "__comment": [
    "Dwarf visual component pools for procedural generation.",
    "",
    "GENERATION MODEL:",
    "  Each dwarf is assigned one value from every applicable pool at generation time.",
    "  Shared pools apply to both genders. Gender-specific pools are separate.",
    "  All selections use the world seed + dwarf birth-order index as the RNG root,",
    "  so the same world always produces the same dwarf appearances in the same order.",
    "",
    "MAP MESH vs. PORTRAIT:",
    "  Two visual representations exist for each dwarf:",
    "    map_mesh    — the 3.3-block character seen walking around the colony.",
    "                  Only broad features are visible: skin tone, hair colour,",
    "                  hair silhouette, and beard presence/absence.",
    "    portrait    — detailed close-up shown in the labour UI and dwarf inspect panel.",
    "                  All appearance fields are rendered here.",
    "",
    "WEIGHT FIELDS:",
    "  Each option entry may include a 'weight' field (default 1 if omitted).",
    "  The generator normalises weights and rolls a weighted random selection.",
    "  Higher weight = more common. Rare options have weight < 1.",
    "",
    "AGE TIERS:",
    "  Visual age tier is cosmetic only — it does not affect stats or lifespan.",
    "  Young dwarves have smoother skin; Elder dwarves have deeper wrinkles and",
    "  white or grey hair streaks. Age tier is assigned independently of trait or",
    "  profession — a young dwarf can be an expert miner if the trait allows it.",
    "",
    "SCAR OVERLAY:",
    "  Scars are a portrait-only overlay drawn on top of the face mesh.",
    "  'none' means no scar overlay is applied (most common).",
    "  Scar models are shared between genders."
  ],

  "shared": {

    "skin_tone": [

{
  "__comment": [
    "Dwarf name component pools for procedural generation.",
    "",
    "GENERATION MODEL:",
    "  Every dwarf receives a single given name constructed as:",
    "    name = prefix + suffix",
    "  Male and female pools are separate — different phoneme patterns.",
    "  Male names lean on hard stops and voiced fricatives (Brom-, Dur-, Grun-).",
    "  Female names lean on softer endings and liquid consonants (Brun-, Kel-, Sol-).",
    "",
    "  Pool sizes:",
    "    Male:   25 prefixes × 20 suffixes = 500 distinct names",
    "    Female: 25 prefixes × 20 suffixes = 500 distinct names",
    "    Total:  1 000 distinct names (500 per gender)",
    "",
    "UNIQUENESS HANDLING:",
    "  The generator tracks used names in the current world. If a rolled combination",
    "  has already been assigned, it re-rolls up to 10 times before falling back to",
    "  appending the dwarf's birth-order index as a Roman numeral suffix",
    "  (e.g. 'Bromin II'). This fallback is expected to be extremely rare — at the",
    "  point where ~500 same-gender dwarves have been generated the pool is",
    "  effectively exhausted, which requires a very long-running colony.",
    "",
    "  Name generation uses the world seed as its RNG root so the same world always",
    "  produces the same sequence of dwarf names in the same order.",
    "",
    "PHONEME NOTES:",
    "  Not every prefix+suffix pair is equally euphonic — that is intentional.",
    "  Dwarven names in this world are guttural and idiosyncratic. A name like",
    "  'Snoruk' or 'Bogorn' is as valid as 'Thorin' or 'Durmar'."
  ],

  "male": {
    "prefixes": [
      "Brom", "Dur",  "Kel",  "Grun", "Thor",
      "Grim", "Bald", "Dug",  "Fur",  "Kor",
      "Ral",  "Snor", "Tek",  "Ulv",  "Var",
      "Horg", "Ber",  "Dal",  "Orm",  "Mund",
      "Rog",  "Skal", "Wulf", "Dral", "Bog"
    ],
    "suffixes": [
      "in",   "an",   "ik",   "ur",   "ak",
      "orn",  "ek",   "as",   "uk",   "grim",
      "rek",  "dor",  "tin",  "bur",  "gar",
      "din",  "mar",  "lok",  "bar",  "dun"
    ]
  },

  "female": {
    "prefixes": [
      "Tho",  "Brun", "Kel",  "Hil",  "Sig",
      "Ing",  "Bryn", "Aud",  "Alf",  "Ger",
      "Val",  "Frid", "Run",  "Ulv",  "Dag",
      "Mor",  "Ast",  "Eld",  "Sol",  "Bir",
      "Gun",  "Hem",  "Ild",  "Lyn",  "Drun"
    ],
    "suffixes": [
      "a",    "ra",   "da",   "na",   "wyn",
      "dis",  "dra",  "ka",   "la",   "tha",
      "dris", "bra",  "fen",  "gra",  "lin",
      "mir",  "sha",  "tris", "vin",  "brin"
    ]
  }
}

extends Node

## Cosmetic voxel flipbook, independent of calendar speed/heat. Only installed
## lights create this node. Meshes are shared; each torch owns its emission material.
## Visibility changes suspend the update loop when the slice hides the parent.
static var _clip_cache: Dictionary = {} # resource path -> named Mesh resources

var _owner: Node3D
var _flame: MeshInstance3D
var _light: OmniLight3D
var _material: StandardMaterial3D
var _frames: Array[Mesh] = []
var _durations: Array[float] = []
var _cycle: float = 0.0
var _elapsed: float = 0.0
var _accum: float = 0.0
var _phase: float = 0.0
var _speed: float = 1.0
var _frame_index: int = -1
var _base_energy: float
var _base_emission: float
var _light_variation: float
var _emission_variation: float
var _frequency: float
var _interval: float


func setup(owner_node: Node3D, flame: MeshInstance3D, light: OmniLight3D,
		material: StandardMaterial3D, config: Dictionary) -> bool:
	set_process(false)
	var clip := _load_clip(String(config.get("model", "")))
	var names: Array = config.get("frames", [])
	var durations: Array = config.get("frame_durations", [])
	if names.is_empty() or names.size() != durations.size():
		push_error("FurnitureFlameAnimation: frame names and durations must match.")
		return false
	for i in range(names.size()):
		var mesh := clip.get(String(names[i])) as Mesh
		var duration := float(durations[i])
		if mesh == null or duration <= 0.0:
			push_error("FurnitureFlameAnimation: missing frame or non-positive duration.")
			return false
		_frames.append(mesh)
		_durations.append(duration)
		_cycle += duration
	_owner = owner_node
	_flame = flame
	_light = light
	_material = material
	_base_energy = light.light_energy
	_base_emission = material.emission_energy_multiplier
	_light_variation = clampf(float(config.get("light_variation", 0)), 0.0, 1.0)
	_emission_variation = clampf(float(config.get("emission_variation", 0)), 0.0, 1.0)
	_frequency = maxf(float(config.get("flicker_frequency_hz", 1)), 0.0)
	_interval = 1.0 / maxf(float(config.get("update_hz", 30)), 1.0)
	# A fixed position-derived phase makes neighbors independent and restores
	# predictable starts without RNG or persisted cosmetic animation state.
	var at := owner_node.global_position * 8.0
	var seed_value := hash(Vector3i(roundi(at.x), roundi(at.y), roundi(at.z))) & 0x7FFFFFFF
	_phase = float(seed_value % 4093) / 4093.0
	var speed_variation := clampf(float(config.get("speed_variation", 0)), 0.0, .5)
	_speed = 1.0 + (float((seed_value >> 12) % 4093) / 4093.0 * 2.0 - 1.0) * speed_variation
	_elapsed = _phase * _cycle
	_apply_sample()
	_owner.visibility_changed.connect(_sync_visibility)
	_sync_visibility()
	return true


static func _load_clip(path: String) -> Dictionary:
	if _clip_cache.has(path):
		return _clip_cache[path]
	if path.is_empty() or not ResourceLoader.exists(path):
		push_error("FurnitureFlameAnimation: missing clip '%s'." % path)
		return {}
	var scene := load(path) as PackedScene
	if scene == null:
		return {}
	var model := scene.instantiate()
	var result := {}
	for mesh: MeshInstance3D in model.find_children("*", "MeshInstance3D", true, false):
		result[String(mesh.name)] = mesh.mesh
	model.free()
	_clip_cache[path] = result
	return result


func _sync_visibility() -> void:
	set_process(_owner.is_visible_in_tree())


func _process(delta: float) -> void:
	if not is_instance_valid(_owner) or not _owner.is_visible_in_tree():
		return
	_elapsed += delta * _speed
	_accum += delta
	if _accum < _interval:
		return
	_accum = fmod(_accum, _interval)
	_apply_sample()


func _apply_sample() -> void:
	var position_in_cycle := fposmod(_elapsed, _cycle)
	var index := 0
	while index < _durations.size() - 1 and position_in_cycle >= _durations[index]:
		position_in_cycle -= _durations[index]
		index += 1
	if index != _frame_index:
		_frame_index = index
		_flame.mesh = _frames[index]
	# Unequal frequencies avoid a regular brightness pulse; the weighted sum
	# stays within [-1,1], keeping both light and emission variation bounded.
	var t := (_elapsed + _phase * 17.0) * TAU * _frequency
	var wave := .55 * sin(t) + .30 * sin(t * 1.91 + _phase * TAU) + .15 * sin(t * .73)
	_light.light_energy = _base_energy * (1.0 + _light_variation * wave)
	_material.emission_energy_multiplier = _base_emission * (1.0 + _emission_variation * wave)

extends RefCounted

## Installed visuals only: caller supplies the definition from the furniture owner.
## Keeping the flame a named mesh avoids making the iron and wood glow too.
static func attach(node: Node3D, def: Dictionary) -> void:
	var light_def: Dictionary = def.get("light_source", {})
	if light_def.is_empty():
		return
	var light := OmniLight3D.new()
	light.name = "FurnitureLight"
	light.light_color = Color(String(light_def.get("color", "#FFFFFF")))
	light.light_energy = float(light_def.get("energy", 1.0))
	light.omni_range = float(light_def.get("range", 5.0))
	light.omni_attenuation = float(light_def.get("attenuation", 1.0))
	light.shadow_enabled = bool(light_def.get("shadows", true))
	var pos: Array = light_def.get("position", [0, 0, 0])
	light.position = Vector3(float(pos[0]), float(pos[1]), float(pos[2]))
	node.add_child(light)
	var mesh_name := String(light_def.get("emissive_mesh", ""))
	for mesh: MeshInstance3D in node.find_children("*", "MeshInstance3D", true, false):
		# A point approximation inside a small lamp creates an oversized black
		# fan from its own bracket. The mount receives light but does not shadow
		# itself; terrain, dwarves and other furniture still cast real shadows.
		mesh.cast_shadow = GeometryInstance3D.SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_OFF
		if String(mesh.name) != mesh_name:
			continue
		var material := StandardMaterial3D.new()
		material.vertex_color_use_as_albedo = true
		material.roughness = 1.0
		material.cull_mode = BaseMaterial3D.CULL_DISABLED
		material.emission_enabled = true
		material.emission = Color.WHITE
		material.emission_operator = BaseMaterial3D.EMISSION_OP_MULTIPLY
		material.emission_energy_multiplier = float(light_def.get("emission_energy", 1.0))
		mesh.material_override = material
		var animation_def: Dictionary = light_def.get("flame_animation", {})
		if not animation_def.is_empty():
			var animation := preload("FurnitureFlameAnimation.gd").new()
			animation.name = "FlameAnimation"
			node.add_child(animation)
			if not animation.setup(node, mesh, light, material, animation_def):
				animation.queue_free() # retain the static glow if a custom clip is invalid
